title: Miri Standard Check Definition
description: Schema for the per-check definition files in standards/<target>/checks/ - the committee-owned, machine-readable source of truth for every check, consumed by linter implementations

id.description: Stable check ID; never renumbered. Extension (health-only) checks use the MIRI-PYX-/MIRI-CLIX- namespaces.

name.description: Short human-readable name of the check

target.description: Artifact type this alert applies to

status.description: Withdrawn checks keep their file and ID; their weight is redistributed in a minor version

added_in.description: Checklist version that introduced this check

withdrawn_in.description: Checklist version that withdrew this check; required when status is withdrawn

level.description: MUST failures make the artifact non-conforming (score capped at 74)

category.description: Checklist category the check belongs to

weight.description: Conformance-score weight; all active weights per target sum to exactly 100. Extension (X-namespace) checks carry weight 0.

conditional.description: Conditional checks score their full weight automatically when the condition does not apply

severity.description: Committee-assigned severity for health scoring; implementations MUST use these values, not their own

default.description: Severity of each violation of this check (numeric values 1-5 in the same order)

violation_unit.description: What counts as one violation - the countable unit that feeds magnitude-aware health scoring

population_unit.description: Committee-defined countable population for per-instance checks (the denominator for report-level violation_density). Defined only where a natural population exists; reports MUST carry the population count when this field is present, and MUST omit it otherwise. Never an input to any score.

short_description.description: One-line statement of what the check verifies

references.description: Standards trail: the specs and external standards this check derives from

examples.description: Concrete examples of the check failing and passing

violation.description: A concrete example of a violation

compliant.description: What the conforming state looks like

requirements.description: Operating capabilities beyond the target's baseline analysis mode (static inspection for wheels; local invocation for CLIs) that this check needs. A linter lacking a listed capability MUST skip the check (forfeited, reported) with the fixed reason: network -> network_unavailable, previous-release -> previous_release_unavailable, execution -> execution_disabled; a linter satisfying them MUST NOT skip. Absent or empty means computable from the artifact alone - skipping is non-conforming.
